introduction: ERC-165 defines a standard method to detect which interfaces a smart contract supports. It introduces a single function, supportsInterface, that takes a 4-byte interface identifier and returns a boolean. This allows contracts and dApps to query whether a target contract implements a specific interface before attempting to interact with it. The standard itself must return true for the ERC-165 interface ID (0x01ffc9a7) and false for 0xffffffff.
designPurpose: ERC-165 was designed to solve the problem of interface discovery on Ethereum. Without it, callers had no reliable way to determine whether a contract supports a particular set of functions, leading to failed calls and wasted gas. By providing a standardized detection mechanism, ERC-165 enables safer contract interactions and is a prerequisite for many other standards like ERC-721 and ERC-1155.
commonUsage: ERC-165 is used extensively by NFT marketplaces, token contracts, and protocol routers to verify that a target contract implements the expected interface. For example, a marketplace can check if a contract supports ERC-721 before attempting to transfer an NFT. It is also used by proxy patterns and modular smart accounts to advertise supported capabilities.
fn.supportsInterface.desc: Returns true if the contract implements the interface defined by the given 4-byte identifier. The interface ID is calculated as the XOR of all function selectors in the interface.
fn.supportsInterface.params.interfaceId: The 4-byte interface identifier to query, as defined in ERC-165. Computed as the XOR of all function selectors in the interface.
fn.supportsInterface.returns.supported: True if the contract implements the queried interface, false otherwise.
sec.trust.title: Interface support is self-reported
sec.trust.desc: supportsInterface answers come from the queried contract itself, so a malicious or buggy contract can claim interfaces it does not implement — or answer true to every query.
sec.trust.mitigation: Treat the answer as a hint, not a proof. Per the specification, a compliant contract must return false for 0xffffffff — query it to filter out contracts that blindly answer true, and keep validating actual call behaviour.
code.iface.title: Canonical ERC-165 interface
gas.notes: The specification caps supportsInterface at under 30,000 gas. Implementations should answer with a constant-time check (a pre-registered mapping or hard-coded comparisons) rather than any unbounded computation.
sim.interfaceQuery.name: Interface Detection Query
sim.interfaceQuery.desc: Query a contract to check whether it supports a specific interface using the supportsInterface function.
sim.interfaceQuery.step.call: The caller invokes supportsInterface(interfaceId) on the target contract to check if a specific interface is supported.
sim.interfaceQuery.step.lookup: The contract looks up the interface ID in its internal registry mapping. Each supported interface is pre-registered during construction.
sim.interfaceQuery.step.return: The contract returns a boolean result. The caller can now safely proceed if the interface is supported, or handle the unsupported case gracefully.
